page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.8xlarge is a high clock speed instance provisioned with 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores, powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a base clock speed of 3.1 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via KVM virtualization, it includes 128 GB of system memory, matching a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. The processor architecture incorporates 35 MB of L3 cache alongside hardware support for AVX, AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, AES, and FMA instructions.

Storage and networking configurations are structured around cloud integration. The instance does not bundle local disk or NVMe storage, requiring external cloud block storage for persistent state. Network performance is anchored by a 10 Gbps baseline bandwidth. In synthetic throughput assessments, large-block memory read bandwidth reached 109.89 GB/sec with write bandwidth at 48.22 GB/sec, while cached small-block reads peaked at 1705.41 GB/sec.

Benchmark evaluations position the ecs.hfg6.8xlarge consistently within average mid-tier cloud server metrics. It achieved a multi-core Geekbench score of 11,107.0, a PassMark CPU score of 29,517.51, and handled 28.91 million Redis SET operations per second alongside 21.45 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU-only machine learning inference delivered 45.98 tokens per second on prompt processing and 12.4 tokens per second on generation with a 7B parameter model. Lacking bundled GPUs, the server provides a balanced, cost-efficient computing environment suited for software compilation, caching layers, application backends, and network-attached database hosting.

Built on x86_64 architecture under KVM, it provides 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores, paired with 128 GB of RAM at a balanced 1:4 ratio. Hardware instructions include AVX-512 and VNNI for vectorized execution, complemented by 35 MB of L3 cache. The instance features a 10 Gbps network baseline and includes no local disks, relying on external network storage. Benchmark results place its multi-core compute in the middle tier, yielding a PassMark CPU score of 29,517.51 and 28.91 million Redis SET operations per second. With balanced compute and memory capacity but no GPU accelerators, ecs.hfg6.8xlarge offers cost-efficient scaling for multi-threaded build pipelines, web application serving, in-memory caching, and general compute-heavy workloads.
